actions.name: See your accounts and balances
actions.summary: Lists this instance's accounts on every configured chain — the EVM account, the demo mock shielded chain, and a public and a private LEZ account — and reads each balance. Every balance is graded attested (the provider's word); a failed read is an error, never a zero. Nothing is agreed.

requirements.target: the EVM RPC in Settings (the hosted wallet is fixed to evm:31337)

requirements.name: lez-sequencer
requirements.target: the LEZ sequencer, through lez_core (real core only)

steps.does: wallet_accounts lists each chain's accounts: EVM (evm:31337, the keystore's secp address), the mock chain (a demo, seeded with balances), and the LEZ (one public and one private account from lez_core; each LEZ row carries share, the address to hand out to be paid). A chain that cannot answer adds {chain, error} instead of emptying the list. wallet_balances reads every account × asset: EVM through eth_getBalance (ETH) on the user's RPC, the LEZ through lez_core's get_balance. Each entry carries grade: attested.

refusals.what: reporting a failed or unanswerable read as a zero balance
refusals.why: the read raises and the entry carries an error (the LEZ's empty-string convention included)

refusals.what: hanging on, or trusting, an unreachable RPC
refusals.why: it raises WalletError

actions.ui: the Main.qml wallet card (each balance with its grade badge) and LezSend.qml

claims.claim: A failed read is reported as an error, never as a zero balance.
Balances are the provider's word (attested) unless checked against a state root.
The RPC provider sees which addresses you read, and when.

evidence.what: moduleWallet: the chains the hosted wallet registers

unverified: The EVM balance read is tested only for parsing and for the unreachable-RPC failure; no test reads a live node.

With MUSTER_LEZ_REAL set, the first wallet call in each process creates a new public LEZ account (and registers it on chain) and a new private one: LezAdapter caches accounts in memory only (lez_adapter.nim accounts, lez_lp.nim createAccount). Read from source; not run.

actions.name: Send ETH from your own account
actions.summary: Sends ETH from this instance's account on the configured EVM chain. The hosted wallet_send is fixed to evm:31337 and submits with eth_sendTransaction, so the node signs for an unlocked account (anvil). Client-side EIP-155 signing through the keystore is built and proven, but the hosted wallet does not select it, so on any other node the hosted send fails. No UI sends ETH. Nobody else approves a wallet send, so there is no agreement field.

requirements.target: evm:31337 (fixed in the hosted wallet)

requirements.name: rpc
requirements.target: the EVM RPC in Settings

requirements.target: hosted path: an account the node has unlocked; client-signing path: the keystore's secp256k1 key

requirements.target: evm:31337 — a 20-byte address

steps.does: wallet_estimate_fee("evm:31337", to, "ETH", raw) returns the RPC's gas price × 21 000.

wallet_send("evm:31337", from, to, "ETH", raw): prepareTransfer builds {to, value}. Hosted path (fromUnlocked, what muster_module builds): eth_sendTransaction(from, to, value, gas 100 000) and the node signs. Client-signing path (fromUnlocked = false): read the nonce and gas price from the RPC, build an EIP-155 legacy transaction (gas 21 000), sign it through the keystore, and broadcast the raw bytes with eth_sendRawTransaction.
steps.signs: Hosted path: nothing — the node signs. Client-signing path: the keystore's secp256k1 key signs keccak256(RLP(nonce, gasPrice, gasLimit, to, value, data, chainId, 0, 0)); V = recid + 2·chainId + 35.

steps.does: The chain includes the transaction; from, to and value become public.
wallet_finality("evm:31337", txHash) reads the receipt: status 1 is final, 0 failed, no receipt pending. Observed, never asserted.

refusals.what: an asset symbol the wallet does not hold
refusals.why: {error: unknown asset}

refusals.what: an unreachable RPC
refusals.why: it raises WalletError; nothing is reported as sent

claims.claim: On the hosted path the node, not the keystore, signs: the RPC must hold the key.
On the client-signing path the key never leaves the keystore, and the signed bytes match the canonical EIP-155 vector.
The RPC provider sees the whole transaction before the chain does.
A legacy transaction binds the chain id and the nonce but carries no expiry.

moduleWallet: newEvmAdapter("evm:31337", rpc) — fromUnlocked defaults to true

actions.name: Read a balance verified against a state root
actions.summary: Upgrades a balance from attested to verified-locally (F-10): the untrusted RPC's eth_getProof is checked against a state root, in process, with nim-eth's verifyMptProof — the Nimbus verified-proxy core. The check is built and tested. The trusted state root is the caller's to supply: the beacon light-client sidecar that would make it trustless is not built. The hosted method is fixed to evm:31337 and nothing in the UI calls it. Nothing is agreed.

requirements.name: rpc
requirements.target: an EVM RPC that serves eth_getProof

requirements.name: trusted-state-root
requirements.target: a consensus-verified execution state root — the beacon light-client sidecar is not built; the caller supplies it

steps.does: wallet_verified_balance(account, stateRoot) fetches eth_getProof(account, latest) from the RPC and verifies the account's Merkle-Patricia proof against stateRoot. A valid proof returns {display, raw, grade: verified-locally}. A proven-absent account is a verified zero. A proof that does not verify returns {error}.

refusals.what: a provider's balance that does not match the state root
refusals.why: the proof fails and the read raises; the number is never trusted

actions.ui: headless only (the Main.qml wallet card has a 'verified' badge, but wallet_balances always returns attested)

claims.claim: A provider whose answer does not match the state root is refused, never trusted.

verifiedBalance: eth_getProof then verify

actions.name: Set up a LEZ account (fallback)
actions.summary: Ensures this instance has a public LEZ account and says whether it holds native LEZ, driving lez_core directly (exo-44b). It funds nothing: LEZ v0.3 removed the testnet's faucet and account registration (exo-eb6.4), and a fresh public account is claimed on chain by its first funded transfer, from someone who holds native LEZ. It is the fallback: delegating setup to the LEZ Wallet App is preferred when the Basecamp broker exists. It runs on the deterministic FakeLezCore by default. The real lez_core path (LpLezCore) is used only when MUSTER_LEZ_REAL is set and lez_core is loaded, and it falls back to the fake if lez_core cannot be reached. Nobody else approves a wallet send, so there is no agreement field.

Returns {account, state: met | missing | unknown, detail}: met once it holds native LEZ, missing with the account someone who holds native LEZ must send to, unknown when the zone cannot be read. The keys stay in lez_core.

actions.name: Receive LEZ: share an address, find the note by scanning
actions.summary: To be paid, you share a public account id (names you as payee) or your shielded key node (does not). A shielded payment lands at a fresh account derived from your key node and an identifier the sender picks, not at an id you published, so you find it by scanning. The scan is built and tested in the adapter, but no hosted wallet method calls it: wallet_accounts and wallet_balances list only the two accounts this instance created, so a note received from another instance does not appear through the wallet surface. The private split's pump does scan, and on the LEZ testnet it found a note another instance sent (scripts/split-lez-testnet.sh, 2026-09-28). It runs on the deterministic FakeLezCore by default. The real lez_core path (LpLezCore) is used only when MUSTER_LEZ_REAL is set and lez_core is loaded, and it falls back to the fake if lez_core cannot be reached. Tests run the fake core; the real path has run on testnet.lez.logos.co in scripts/split-lez-testnet.sh. Nobody else approves a wallet send, so there is no agreement field.

steps.does: wallet_accounts gives each LEZ account a share field: the public account's id, or the private account's key node priv:<npk>:<vpk> (read with get_private_account_keys). Which one you hand out is your disclosure choice; LezSend.qml offers both to copy.

syncPrivate() walks lez_core's scan toward the chain tip in bounded steps (get_current_block_height, get_last_synced_block, sync_to_block of at most 250 blocks per call — a fresh wallet starts at block 0, and one jump to the tip outlives the call) and lists the private accounts now discoverable; a received note shows its balance, at exactly the amount sent, against the discovered account, under the key node it was sent to. Polling the published id does not work for a shielded payment. No hosted wallet method calls syncPrivate; the private split's pump scans through the same adapter.

actions.name: Pay someone on the LEZ: request, share, send (Mode A)
actions.summary: The default LEZ payment. The payer asks, the recipient shares an address, the payer sends. No approval and no threshold: the coordination is the exchange of an address, and the form the recipient shares picks the rail and the privacy. When a room wants members to approve k-of-n before lez_core runs the transfer (Mode B), that is the family action room.invoke/lez-transfer, not this. It runs on the deterministic FakeLezCore by default. The real lez_core path (LpLezCore) is used only when MUSTER_LEZ_REAL is set and lez_core is loaded, and it falls back to the fake if lez_core cannot be reached. Tests run the fake core. The real path has run on testnet.lez.logos.co: wallet_send shielded a faucet claim to the sender's own key node (a ~6-minute proof) in scripts/split-lez-testnet.sh. Nobody else approves a wallet send, so there is no agreement field.
